d: Convert any oven recipe to an air fryer: lower the temperature about 25°F / 15°C, cut the time about 20 percent, and know when conversion fails.

The fix is three adjustments. They are rules of thumb, not a formula. Air fryer models differ in wattage, basket size and how close the element sits to the food. Treat every time below as a range, and verify doneness with an instant-read thermometer. The three general rules Rule one: lower the temperature by roughly 25°F / 15°C. Air fryer dials are usually calibrated at the element, not at the food, and the food sits much closer to it. Rule two: cut the time by roughly 20 percent. A 25–30 min oven step becomes about 20–24 min. Rule three: check early. Open the basket at about two-thirds of the converted time. Once something is over-browned, there is no way back. Two constraints matter as much as the numbers. The basket holds one layer, so a sheet-pan recipe becomes two or three rounds. And most air fryers need a 3–5 min preheat for browning.
